question.text: Motion of a particle in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></math> plane is described by a set of following equations <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The path of the particle will be

solution.text:
x=4sinπ2-ωt=4cosωt,

y=4sinωt

Clearly,   x2+y2=4cosωt2+4sinωt2⇒x2+y2=16

Hence, the path covered by particle is a circle.
